- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) in the last 1–2 days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to match sentiment-driven momentum.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) in the last 1–2 days, model tends to overreact — reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.  
- Model consistently overestimates near the end of the 30-day horizon (last 5–7 days) — apply downward bias to final 5–7 forecast points.  
- When sentiment is neutral (0.0) and price is trending upward, model often lags — add 1–2% lagged momentum to forecast.  
- If recent history shows sharp upward spikes (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model tends to overshoot — cap forecast at 10–15% above peak for 3–5 days.  
- Model underestimates mean reversion in volatile periods — if 3–5 consecutive days show high volatility, apply 1–2% upward adjustment to mean-reversion target.  
- If sentiment is positive but price is flat or declining, model often overcorrects — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% to avoid false bullishness.
